questions.q: What is an Application Accounting Definition (AAD)?
options: A single journal line rule for one event type
A complete, named accounting configuration that bundles every journal entry rule set (and related description rules and supporting references) for one subledger application
A report listing every GL account in the Chart of Accounts
A synonym for the General Ledger
questions.explain: An AAD packages all the rule sets for one subledger application, like Payables, into one coherent, versionable object.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of bundling rule sets into an AAD rather than assigning them individually?
options: There is no advantage; it only adds extra steps
An accounting method only needs to reference one AAD per subledger application, instead of hand-assembling dozens of individual rule sets
It eliminates the need for account rules
It removes the need for a Chart of Accounts
questions.explain: Bundling simplifies assignment: the accounting method references one AAD per application rather than many separate rule sets.

questions.q: What tool is used to build and manage AADs, journal line rules, account rules, description rules, and supporting references?
options: The Accounting Methods Builder (AMB)
Microsoft Excel
The Chart of Accounts Designer
The Payables Invoice Workbench
questions.explain: The Accounting Methods Builder is the tool where all of Chapter 2's rule types, and the AAD that bundles them, are configured.

questions.q: In the Payables AAD example, what did the AAD contain?
options: Only a single rule for the Invoices event class, with no other content
Journal entry rule sets for multiple event classes, such as Invoices, Payments, and Prepayments
The entire Receivables configuration as well
A list of every supplier in the system
questions.explain: The example Payables AAD bundled rule sets for the Invoices, Payments, and Prepayments event classes into one named package.

questions.q: How does an AAD relate to the accounting method covered in lesson 3?
options: They are unrelated concepts from different products
The accounting method points to one AAD per subledger application; the AAD is the object at that "per subledger application" layer
An accounting method contains dozens of AADs for every possible ledger in the world
AADs replace accounting methods entirely in recent Fusion releases
questions.explain: The accounting method references an AAD for each subledger application; the AAD is the complete rule bundle for that one application.
